findings.title: Duplicate test module basename breaks full-tree pytest collection
findings.defect: Both new adapter suites are non-package files named test_backend_adapter.py. Default pytest imports the coverage file under that name, then refuses to collect the mutation file.
findings.scenario: Run python3.12 -m pytest -q tools/ci/tests on the frozen candidate: exit 2, import file mismatch. Clean archives reproduce base collection exit 0 (39 cases) versus candidate exit 2 (63 collected plus one error), ruling out the pre-existing worktree caches.
findings.reproducer: python3.12 -m pytest -q tools/ci/tests; compare python3.12 -m pytest --collect-only -q tools/ci/tests on git archives of base and candidate.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the mutation adapter suite a unique basename and verify whole-tree collection. Do not casually add __init__.py: that would also make the normal unittest gate recurse into native-tool suites, changing its prerequisites.
findings.origin_escape: Introduced by G01 adapter controls, not by bug1. Per-directory qualification and top-level unittest discovery cannot expose cross-directory pytest module collisions. The bug1 receipt correctly calls it pre-existing relative to bug1, but that does not make it baseline debt for this review.

findings.title: Final exec bypasses mutation workspace cleanup
findings.defect: The wrapper installs an EXIT trap at line 21 but exec replaces the shell before it can run. Every completed native mutation run leaves its archived backend and mutants tree on disk.
findings.scenario: Set TMPDIR to a fresh owned directory and run the existing known-killed fixture. The adapter returns 0, yet one newly created work directory remains containing backend/ and backend/mutants/.
findings.reproducer: Use BackendMutationAdapter.setUp(), set TMPDIR to an isolated directory, snapshot its children, run_adapter with CONTROL and BOTH, then compare children after return; inspect only the newly created child. Native result: exit 0, LEAKED_WORKDIR_COUNT 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Call the evaluator without exec and exit with its status so EXIT cleanup runs on PASS, FAIL and GAP; verify cleanup of only the owned workspace.
findings.origin_escape: The checkout-is-unchanged assertion checks the source repo, not the separately allocated mktemp workspace.

findings.title: Stale XML for an existing file can falsely pass changed-line coverage
findings.defect: Completeness validation checks only that each changed filename appears in diff-cover src_stats. It does not bind the XML to the source revision or ensure that newly added executable lines are represented.
findings.scenario: Generate real 100% XML for control.py, commit a candidate that changes one previously covered return and adds an untested function, then evaluate the old XML against the new candidate. It returns PASS/0 at 100% over one line. Running the native wrapper afresh on the same candidate returns FAIL/1 at 66% over three lines.
findings.reproducer: Use BackendCoverageAdapter with CONTROL/BOTH to generate XML; preserve XML; set base to that HEAD; commit CONTROL.replace("covered", "new") plus def untested(): return "new logic", and update the covered assertion. Invoke evaluate.py BASE STALE_XML OUT, then backend.sh BASE OUT. Observed exits 0 then 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind native evidence to candidate/source digests and reject mismatched reports, and/or compare report statements with a candidate executable-line inventory. Add a stale-same-file control, not just the existing newly-added-file control.
findings.origin_escape: The existing stale-XML test adds an entirely new file, so filename presence is enough to pass that test while missing the stated stale-report obligation.

findings.title: Incomplete mutation inventory is accepted as complete evidence
findings.defect: The parser accepts any nonempty inventory with one matching module and scores independent aggregate stats. It never reconciles parsed IDs/statuses with total or status counts. The wrapper also ignores the export/results command status at line 31.
findings.scenario: A real native run produces four killed mutant IDs and total=4. Retain only the first native inventory line, preserving the native stats. The evaluator returns PASS/0 with mutants=1, killed=4 and total=4. An interrupted or partially written results export can therefore omit survivors or unresolved cases without invalidating the score.
findings.reproducer: After the real CONTROL/BOTH adapter run, truncate mutmut-results.txt to its first __mutmut_ line; invoke python3 tools/ci/mutation/evaluate.py OUT backend/src/control.py 0. Observed PASS/0 with inconsistent counts.
findings.suggested_fix: Require successful export and results commands, validate supported schema/statuses, and reconcile all unique IDs and per-status counts with native totals before scoring. Reject missing, truncated or inconsistent inventory as GAP.
findings.origin_escape: Controls cover an absent/empty inventory, timeout and absent file mapping, but not partial native inventory or exporter failure.

findings.title: Unchanged functions dilute the changed-behavior mutation score
findings.defect: only_mutate selects whole changed files, and evaluate.py scores every native mutant in those files. The approved denominator is changed executable behavior, not all behavior in a file that happened to change.
findings.scenario: Start with two unchanged, fully tested functions (eight killed mutants), then add only one untested function to their file (two no-tests mutants). The adapter returns PASS/0 at 80%, although zero of the two mutants in the actual changed behavior are killed.
findings.reproducer: Commit CONTROL plus CONTROL renamed verdict2, with BOTH tests for each. Set base to that commit. Append only def untested(): return "untested" and run backend.sh BASE OUT. Native result: killed=8, no_tests=2, PASS 80%; both new function mutants are listed as no tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind selected native mutant IDs to changed executable behavior/functions before calculating the score, preserving full inventory for review. If the admitted backend cannot establish this mapping, return a named scope GAP instead of a whole-file PASS.
findings.origin_escape: All positive/negative fixtures introduce an entire new source file, so they never distinguish changed behavior from previously tested code.

findings.title: A function mutant masks unsupported module-level changes in the same file
findings.defect: The unmapped check requires only one mutant anywhere in each changed module. It therefore loses the required PYTHON_NONFUNCTION_MUTATION_GAP when unsupported changed module-level behavior coexists with supported functions.
findings.scenario: Add control.py containing LIMIT = 3 followed by the tested CONTROL function, with BOTH tests. Native mutmut emits four function mutants and none for LIMIT, yet the evaluator returns PASS/0 at 100%.
findings.reproducer: Run the admitted adapter against a committed new control.py with "LIMIT = 3\n\n" + CONTROL and BOTH. Native inventory contains only control.x_verdict__mutmut_1..4; result is PASS rather than PYTHON_NONFUNCTION_MUTATION_GAP.
findings.suggested_fix: Inspect changed executable scope and explicitly reject unsupported module-level behavior with the planned typed gap, even when the same file has function mutants. Preserve any exclusions only through explicit approved scope disposition.
findings.origin_escape: The existing negative case puts LIMIT in a separate constants.py file, where filename mapping catches it; it misses mixed supported/unsupported behavior.

findings.title: Action admission PASS conflicts with explicitly stale scanner data
findings.defect: The receipt records Trivy --offline-scan --skip-db-update with a three-day-old database whose NextUpdate has passed (line 6), but grants PASS to both actions (lines 31 and 55). The invoked supply-chain skill requires INDETERMINATE for missing/stale required scanner data; no owner acceptance of this named residual gap appears in the review authority.
findings.scenario: The new setup-java and setup-python workflow pins are admitted based on these PASS claims. Inspection of the receipt reproduces the policy contradiction: stale-required-data guard is false. Disposition of the listed old advisories does not establish that newer advisories are absent.
findings.reproducer: Parse supply-scan.json: scanners.trivy contains "NextUpdate passed" while both actions[*].verdict equal PASS. Compare scan-software-supply-chain/SKILL.md section 6, which classifies stale required scanner data as INDETERMINATE.
findings.suggested_fix: Rerun the affected vulnerability check on the exact action bytes using current admitted advisory data and persist sanitized results with provenance, or correct the verdict to INDETERMINATE and retain the admission hold until explicit owner residual-risk acceptance. Do not label a new scan or acceptance PASS before it exists.
